subject: Mathematics
title: Area & Perimeter of Square
formula: Area = side × side (a²) | Perimeter = 4 × side (4a)
explanation: All 4 sides are equal. Use square units (cm², m²) for area and linear units (cm, m) for perimeter.
example: If side = 6 cm → Area = 36 cm², Perimeter = 24 cm.

subject: Mathematics
title: Area & Perimeter of Rectangle
formula: Area = length × breadth (l × b) | Perimeter = 2 × (l + b)
explanation: Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal. Add length and breadth first, then multiply by 2 for perimeter.
example: l = 8 cm, b = 5 cm → Area = 40 cm², Perimeter = 26 cm.

subject: Mathematics
title: Area of Triangle
formula: Area = (1/2) × base × height
explanation: Height must be perpendicular (90°) to the chosen base. Any triangle's area is half of a parallelogram with the same base and height.
example: base = 10 cm, height = 6 cm → Area = 0.5 × 10 × 6 = 30 cm².

subject: Mathematics
title: Circle Circumference & Area
formula: Circumference = 2πr = πd | Area = πr²
explanation: r is radius, d is diameter (d = 2r), and π ≈ 22/7 or 3.14.
example: r = 7 cm → Circumference = 44 cm, Area = 154 cm².

subject: Mathematics
title: Area of Parallelogram & Trapezium
formula: Parallelogram = b × h | Trapezium = (1/2) × (a + b) × h
explanation: For a trapezium, 'a' and 'b' are the two parallel sides and 'h' is the perpendicular distance between them.
example: Parallel sides 6 cm & 10 cm, h = 4 cm → Area = 0.5 × 16 × 4 = 32 cm².

subject: Mathematics
title: Cube: Surface Area & Volume
formula: TSA = 6a² | LSA = 4a² | Volume = a³
explanation: A cube has 6 equal square faces of edge length 'a'. Volume measures space inside in cubic units.
example: Edge a = 4 cm → TSA = 96 cm², Volume = 64 cm³.

subject: Mathematics
title: Cuboid: Surface Area & Volume
formula: TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl) | Volume = l × b × h
explanation: l = length, b = breadth, h = height. Lateral surface area of 4 walls is 2h(l + b).
example: l = 5, b = 3, h = 2 cm → Volume = 30 cm³, TSA = 62 cm².

subject: Mathematics
title: Right Circular Cylinder
formula: CSA = 2πrh | TSA = 2πr(r + h) | Volume = πr²h
explanation: CSA is the curved outer wrap; TSA adds top and bottom circular bases.
example: r = 7 cm, h = 10 cm → Volume = 1540 cm³.

subject: Mathematics
title: Right Circular Cone & Sphere
formula: Cone Vol = (1/3)πr²h, CSA = πrl | Sphere Vol = (4/3)πr³, SA = 4πr²
explanation: Slant height of a cone satisfies l² = r² + h².
example: A cone has 1/3 the volume of a cylinder with the same radius and height.

subject: Mathematics
title: Pythagoras Theorem
formula: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Height² (c² = a² + b²)
explanation: Applies strictly to right-angled triangles (90°). The hypotenuse is the longest side opposite the right angle.
example: Base = 3, Height = 4 → Hypotenuse = √(9 + 16) = 5.

subject: Mathematics
title: Core Algebraic Identities
formula: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² | (a - b)² = a² - 2ab + b² | a² - b² = (a + b)(a - b)
explanation: Use these identities to expand expressions fast or factorize quadratic terms without long multiplication.

subject: Mathematics
title: Arithmetic Progression (AP) & Quadratic Formula
explanation: In an AP, 'a' is first term and 'd' is common difference. Discriminant D = b² - 4ac shows nature of roots.

subject: Mathematics
title: Basic Trigonometric Ratios & Identity
formula: sin θ = P/H | cos θ = B/H | tan θ = P/B | sin²θ + cos²θ = 1
explanation: For an acute angle θ in a right triangle: P = Perpendicular (opposite), B = Base (adjacent), H = Hypotenuse.
example: tan θ = sin θ / cos θ; also 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

subject: Mathematics
title: Percentage, Profit/Loss & Simple Interest
formula: Profit% = (Profit/CP) × 100 | SI = (P × R × T) / 100
explanation: Profit or loss percentage is always calculated on Cost Price (CP). P = Principal, R = Rate % p.a., T = Time in years.
example: CP = ₹200, SP = ₹250 → Profit = ₹50 → Profit% = 25%.

subject: Science
title: Speed, Force, Work & Ohm's Law
formula: Speed = Distance / Time | Force = m × a | Work = F × d | V = I × R
explanation: SI units: Speed (m/s), Force (Newton, N), Work/Energy (Joule, J), Voltage (Volt, V), Current (Ampere, A), Resistance (Ohm, Ω).
example: Current I = 2 A through R = 5 Ω resistor → Voltage V = 10 V.

subject: Science
title: Mirror Formula, Magnification & Kinetic Energy
explanation: Follow sign convention carefully for concave/convex mirrors; KE depends on mass (m) and square of velocity (v).
example: Doubling speed increases Kinetic Energy by 4 times (2² = 4).

subject: Science
title: Resistivity (ρ) & Electric Power / Energy
formula: Resistivity: Ω·m (Ohm-metre) | Power: W (Watt = J/s) | Energy: J (Joule) or kWh
explanation: Don't confuse Resistance (Ω) with Resistivity (Ω·m)—resistivity is a material property, not dependent on length or area. 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.
example: R = ρ(l/A) → ρ = R·A/l has unit (Ω × m²) / m = Ω·m.

subject: Science
title: Lens Power (Dioptre), Pressure & Frequency
formula: Lens Power: m⁻¹ or Dioptre (D) | Pressure: Pa (Pascal = N/m²) | Frequency: Hz (Hertz = s⁻¹)
explanation: Focal length (f) in Power formula P = 1/f MUST be in metres (m), so 1 D = 1 m⁻¹. Pascal (Pa) equals one Newton per square metre.
example: f = +0.5 m → P = 1 / 0.5 = +2 D (convex lens).

subject: Science
title: Momentum, Impulse, Torque/Moment & Specific Heat
formula: Momentum: kg·m/s (N·s) | Frequency/Decay: s⁻¹ (Hz) | Specific Heat: J/(kg·K)
explanation: Momentum (p = mv) and Impulse (F·Δt) share the exact same SI unit (kg·m/s = N·s). Temperature difference in SI uses Kelvin (K) or °C interval.
example: p = 2 kg × 3 m/s = 6 kg·m/s.

subject: Science
title: Amount of Substance (Mole), Density & Volume
formula: Amount: mol (Mole) | Density: kg/m³ | Volume: m³ (1 m³ = 1000 L)
explanation: While labs often use g/cm³ or mL, the strict SI unit of volume is cubic metre (m³) and density is kg/m³ (1 g/cm³ = 1000 kg/m³).
example: Water density ≈ 1000 kg/m³ = 1 g/cm³.
